images.title: 5 spreadsheet mistakes in your *tax provision*
images.sub: And the fix for each one. Number 4 is the one your auditor asks about.

images.title: Hard-coded 21%
images.text: Someone typed 21% into 400 cells. Then a rate changes – a state rate, a new entity, a blended rate – and half the workbook stays wrong. Quietly.
images.box: One rate table as a parameter. Every cell points to it.

images.title: Broken links → *#REF!*
images.text: Your provision pulls from “Provision_Final_v3_NEW.xlsx”. Someone moved it last Tuesday. You find out in review.
images.box: One data source. Import the data – don’t link files.

images.title: No version history
images.text: Who changed row 48 – and why? In most workbooks, nobody knows. “_v3_FINAL_NEW” is not a version history.
images.box: A change log with date, person and reason – written automatically.

images.title: No audit trail
images.text: The number is right – but where does it come from? Your SOX auditor will ask. “It’s somewhere in tab 7” is not an answer.
images.box: Every number traces back to its source in one click.

images.title: Rounding too early
images.text: Round every line, sum at the end – and you get $1 differences that someone “fixes” by hand. Plugs are where errors hide.
images.box: Calculate at full precision. Round once – at the end.

images.title: I build tools that *prevent* all 5.
images.text: Free demo with sample data, then a 20-min intro call. No coding skills needed.
